newsitem.title: USA: Wachovia to acquire Central Fidelity Banks.
newsitem.headline: Wachovia to acquire Central Fidelity Banks.

text.p: Wachovia Corp. said Tuesday it had agreed to acquire Central Fidelity Banks Inc. in an exchange of stock valued at $2.3 billion.
Wachovia said the deal would make it the leading bank in Virginia and move its national ranking to 17 from 20.
Central Fidelity, the parent of Central Fidelity National Bank in Richmond, Va., had assets of $10.6 billion on March 31 and is Virgina's third largest banking company.

The merger, expected to close in the fourth quarter, has been approved by directors of both companies and is subject to approval by shareholders and appropriate regulatory agencies. The deal is expected to have a positive impact on Wachovia's earnings in 1999, the company said.

The merger agreement provides for a tax-free exchange of 0.63 Wachovia common share each Central Fidelity common share. Based on Wachovia's closing stock price yesterday of $62.625, and Central Fidelity's 58.8 million fully diluted shares, the transaction is worth about $39.45 per Central Fidelity share, or a total of $2.3 billion, Wachovia said.
Wachovia operates mainly in North and South Carolina and Georgia. It recently announced the acquisition of Jefferson Bankshares Inc. of Charlottesville, Va.

The Central Fidelity deal, along with the Jefferson Bancshares transaction, will position Wachovia as the leading bank in Virginia, with 335 branch offices and deposits totaling $9.9 billion, the company said.
On completion of the two deals, Wachovia will have assets of $60.2 billion and a retail banking network of 817 banking offices and 1,134 ATMs.
Central Fidelity has granted Wachovia a stock option representing about 19.9 percent of Central Fidelity's outstanding shares.
Wachovia said both companies have terminated their stock repurchase programs.
